content.comment_body: We have a circular setup with 50 storage shelves that move in both directions and use a shelf 1 proximity sensor. I need to implement an up/down counter that wraps to 0 when counting upward and wraps from 0 to 50 when counting downward. It also needs to reset whenever the shelf 1 sensor is triggered. This value is displayed as the current shelf number. Is there a simple method I'm overlooking, using the standard up/down counter block? I can get the counter to wrap in one direction with the 'start value' and 'on' parameters, but managing wrapping in both directions is proving difficult.

Hello [user_name], Implementing this with just a few blocks isn't straightforward. However, this subject was discussed previously in the German section of the forum, and there are some solutions available for reference. [document] (title translated: Counting in a circle forward and backward) greetings [user_name]

Hi [user_name], Thank you for pointing me to the German forum. It reassured me that my challenges are not unusual. For others' reference, I've attached the solution, translated into English and annotated for clarity.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users explored ways to set up a bi-directional up/down counter with wrap-around functionality using the existing counter block in [product_name] engineering software. The key issue is that built-in blocks don't easily allow wrapping in both directions, pushing users towards community-shared workarounds or custom configurations. Participants acknowledged that this requirement is more challenging than what standard function blocks can intuitively support.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the up/down counter block to support bi-directional wrapping—cycling from the highest to lowest value and vice versa—plus a simple reset triggered by an external sensor, all within an easy-to-configure interface or logic structure.
